_comment: HAND-WRITTEN corpus (the third one here that is not generated from the browser reference). It pins the STATUS half of "could this failed mutation still have committed server-side?" — the question a relay asks before deciding whether a failed vault write is worth reconciling against the server's document. Hand-written because no relay is the oracle: the browser's `isAmbiguousMutationFailure` carries arms the ports have no equivalent for (a CSRF refusal, a caller-initiated abort, the unknown-outcome 409), so generating `ambiguous` from it would dress one port up as the reference for a rule all three own equally. THE RULE: AMBIGUOUS means the server may have acted — no response at all, or a status it could return after the commit. DEFINITE means it answered before mutating, or never saw the request. A null `status` is the no-status-line case (a transport throw) and is ambiguous: a request that never got a status line cannot rule the commit out. SCOPE: statuses and the null case ONLY. Each relay's non-status arms are language-specific — the browser's `CsrfTokenMissingError`/`AbortError`/unknown-outcome-409, the CLI's `VaultError`, macOS's `.invalidKey` and its non-`APIError` fallthrough — and stay in that relay's own unit tests. Consumers: `isAmbiguousMutationFailure` (frontend/src/lib/idempotency.ts), `is_ambiguous_failure` (client/plugin/src/costcompass/api.py), `APIClient.isAmbiguousFailure` (client/macos/.../API/APIClient.swift).

vectors.name: status-none
vectors.why: No status line at all — a transport throw. The request may have been received and committed before the connection died, so it cannot rule the commit out. This is the case the rotation write-back exists to recover.

vectors.name: status-400
vectors.why: The server validated and refused before touching state. Nothing was written.

vectors.name: status-401
vectors.why: Rejected at the auth layer, before the handler ran.

vectors.name: status-403
vectors.why: Rejected at the auth layer, before the handler ran.

vectors.name: status-404
vectors.why: The server answered that the target does not exist; it did not mutate one.

vectors.name: status-408
vectors.why: The server gave up waiting on a request it may already have read in full.

vectors.name: status-409
vectors.why: An ordinary conflict is a definite refusal. (The browser narrows ONE 409 — its idempotency reservation envelope — to ambiguous, and a vault revision conflict is handled before this question is asked at all. Both are body-shaped distinctions, outside this corpus's status-only scope.)

vectors.name: status-413
vectors.why: The body was rejected on size before the handler ran.

vectors.name: status-429
vectors.why: The rate limiter answers ahead of the handler, so nothing was written. Retrying would only burn another token — this is why 429 is NOT lumped in with 5xx.

vectors.name: status-500
vectors.why: The handler may have committed and then failed on the way out.

vectors.name: status-501
vectors.why: 5xx with no more specific rule: assume the server may have acted.

vectors.name: status-502
vectors.why: A gateway reporting an upstream it cannot speak for — the upstream may have run.

vectors.name: status-503
vectors.why: The peer that answered may not be the peer that would have written.

vectors.name: status-504
vectors.why: A gateway that gave up on an upstream still running. The write may yet land.

vectors.name: status-599
vectors.why: The top of the 5xx range holds the same way the bottom does.
